cells.tense: You are here with the whole thing and your own shape holds inside it.
cells.act: bear the next hour of it without deciding anything
cells.ask: While someone's upset is filling the room, stay beside them and carry it alongside for an hour. Don't fix it. Don't decide anything about it. Hold your own outline while it's here. When the hour's up, it's done.
cells.core:
You can stand near someone else's feeling and not fall into it. You know where you end and they begin, and you can hold both at the same time. That's a particular strength: you feel with someone without losing your own shape, and they can tell you're there and not just swept along.

That doesn't mean the pull is weak. When someone is hurting, the old move is to reach in and take it, decide it, fix it so the room gets lighter. What works here is smaller and harder: carry the next hour of it alongside them and decide nothing. Feel it, stay in your own outline, and ride out that stretch with them. You don't have to resolve their feeling to be with them; bearing it is the thing.

cells.tense: You are already wearing the ending of someone else's feeling before it has happened.
cells.act: let the thing end that is already over
cells.ask: Notice whatever's finished between you and someone — a habit of rescuing, a way you've been propping it up. Stop doing that part. No announcement, no relitigating. Just the part that's over, ended.
cells.core:
You can feel what other people feel so directly that the line between you and them goes thin. Their dread arrives and you're already handling it; you plan for it, brace against it, carry their future for them. It looks like care. From inside, it's hard to find where you stop and they start.

What would actually help is smaller and plainer. Between you and someone there's a thing that's already finished — a way of rescuing, a habit of worrying on their behalf — and you're still holding it up. Let that one end. Not the relationship; the piece of it that's done. For a week, when you catch yourself doing it, just don't. The space it leaves is not empty. It's where the next honest thing between you can take its own shape.

cells.tense: You were at the door of feeling with them, and you're still standing where the door used to be.
cells.act: adjust one dial a little, then stop
cells.ask: When you're with someone and it stays at the surface, change how you're doing it — a sentence, a question, a pause. See what shifts. Adjust again or leave it there. No big decision.
cells.core:
You used to be able to feel with people. These days you can see the shape of the exchange from outside and can't feel your way into it. The connections stay at a level that doesn't reach either of you, and neither of you crosses. Trying harder may not be what moves it; that's worth testing.

Something tiny and repeated does. Next time you're with someone, do two things differently and stop — a question, a silence, a sentence truer than the last — and notice what shifted before you do anything else. You're not aiming at Big Feeling. You're finding the setting that lets the room breathe, and the feeling comes back with the breathing. One turn of the dial, then look.
cells.sheetLine: The dial's low. Turn it once and look.

cells.tense: You are the one doing the feeling-with, and your account says you're only watching.
cells.act: trace the pattern across the last few times
cells.ask: Think back over the last times someone came to you and left lighter. In a line or two, write the move you keep making that brings them there. Don't explain it, don't change it — just put it down.
cells.core:
People come to you and feel held. They leave lighter and you're not sure why, or you'd say you only listened. Something is running there that you don't count as yours to claim. Ask you and you were nearby, not the one holding anyone.

Seeing it is what's available, not more feeling. Look at two or three times someone came to you and left better, and find the shape of what you do — the way you stay, the way you don't flinch, the small straight question. Write it as one line. That line is the mechanism, and once you see it you'll find you were inside it the whole time. Naming it doesn't change the doing. It gives you back the author.

attempts.check: The unsupported claim is that the person's numbness or fusion is a standing condition of the capacity rather than a moment; the record only says what the capacity is doing in a recognisable scene. A reader could say 'I'm not numb, I'm just busy,' and the reading needs to survive that. The asks still work if wrong: adjusting one thing, letting one thing end, holding one hour, naming one shape are useful whether or not the diagnosis lands. The sentence that serves the writer more than the person is any line that turns recognition into a verdict on who they are.
